label: conj:shell-space-is-self-square
title: The shell state space is the self-square of the angular object
html:
Conjecture. Write V_j for the \mathrm{SU}(2)_q irrep of spin j, of q-dimension [2j+1]_q, and let j_n = (n-1)/2 be the spin of the angular object of principal shell n, so that \dim_q V_{j_n} = [n]_q. Then the orbital state space of shell n is the self-fusion of that one object with itself,

  \mathcal{O}_n \;\cong\; V_{j_n} \otimes V_{j_n} ,

the second tensor factor being a copy of the first, tied to it by the coproduct. In particular \dim_q \mathcal{O}_n = [n]_q^2.

The spin labelling is the one used in conj:orbital-space-normal-bundle: V_\ell there is the sub-shell irrep of dimension 2\ell+1, which is V_j here at integer j = \ell.

This is the one step of the 2n^2 shell-capacity account that is not derived. Everything downstream of it is exact.

What the conjecture is not. It is not a claim that a second symmetry group acts. The (j,j) doubling that the hydrogenic shell classically receives from \mathrm{SO}(4) = \mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{SU}(2) and its Runge–Lenz vector is here internal to a single object. The compact (\cos/\sin, root of unity) and non-compact (\cosh/\sinh, real q) pictures are the two real forms of one \mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C}), so no second compact \mathrm{SU}(2) is required or postulated.

What follows exactly. Given the identification, the q-Clebsch–Gordan rule decomposes the self-square into the sub-shells,

  V_{j_n} \otimes V_{j_n} \;\cong\; \bigoplus_{\ell=0}^{n-1} V_\ell ,
  \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
  [n]_q^2 \;=\; \sum_{\ell=0}^{n-1} [2\ell+1]_q ,

which is prop:shell-capacity-self-square and, at q = 1, the periodic-table capacities 2n^2 = 2,8,18,32,\ldots. Clearing the common denominator (q - q^{-1}) turns this into a polynomial identity over \mathbb{Z}[q,q^{-1}], proved for every n in the Lean sibling as qCG_self_square. Previously only the q = 1 integer specialisation \sum_{\ell<n}(2\ell+1) = n^2 was formalised; the q-deformed statement had been checked symbolically for n = 1,\ldots,8 in computations/shell_capacity_chebyshev_bridge.py.

Falsifiable content. The conjecture asserts more than a coincidence of counts. It fixes the sub-shell multiplicities as the q-integers [2\ell+1]_q, and not only their q \to 1 values 2\ell+1; a resolved sub-shell structure departing from [2\ell+1]_q at q \neq 1 would refute it. The Lean sibling records this as subshell_decomposition_of_self_square, derived from the conjectural hypothesis rather than assumed alongside it, together with a concrete refuting witness not_selfSquare_linear showing that the class is not satisfied by an arbitrary dimension function.

Relation to the normal-bundle model. conj:orbital-space-normal-bundle describes the same space \mathcal{O}_n geometrically, as framing-k sections of the trefoil's normal bundle in Bring's surface cut off by a q-Laplacian eigenvalue bound. The two are independent descriptions of one object: the present conjecture supplies its categorical structure, the normal-bundle conjecture its geometric realisation. Establishing an isomorphism between them would close both at once.
